notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/table.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/table.md at 622cd82 (“docs: publish 11 Coin fixes on jfs-components v0.1.78-a116616”, 17 October), the same files on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note was checked on 17 October 2026 on the build it calls the 16 October build (mirror v0.1.78-a116616, Biscuit's main at a116616, the #264 fix), so items citing it carry 2026-10-17 and 0.1.78-a116616. The evidence has two checks: 12 October on 636f3f5 (the first check: contract, Figma, Storybook, measurements) and the 17 October re-check on a116616 (#264: body colour, Weight, grid roles, pressable rows). Each item cites its section's own date and build: the re-check paragraph's onRowPress sentence carries 2026-10-17 and 0.1.78-a116616; contract lines unchanged since the first check (git 4fee471 → 622cd82), the empty-data sentence among them, carry 2026-10-12 and 0.1.78-636f3f5; the evidence's Coin gaps section (#264 still To do) is superseded by the re-check and not cited. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). GitHub's compare of v0.1.78-a116616...v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (4 commits, 222 files, complete) changes no Table, Text, react-utils, typography, web-platform-utils or design-tokens file, and the installed Table.tsx is identical to a116616's (fetched with gh api and diffed). Read from source, not run, with token values through the package's own getVariableByName: header cells #f5f5f5 with 14/600 labels on a 20 px line, cells #ffffff with 12 px padding and 1 px #eeeeee lines on the right and below (Table.tsx 62–90, 204–245), one header cell per column and one line under the header (309–326); body text 14 px on a 17 px line at Medium, so a row is 12 + 17 + 12 + 1 = 42 px and the header 45; Context ListItem makes Medium 12 px; values are Regular 400 unless a Weight mode is set (bodyTextModes, 103–106), Bold 800; a cell's width is its column's width, then columnWidth, then flex 1 with minWidth 0 (235, 288); the root has overflow hidden and width 100% unless scrollable (624); scrollable wraps it in a horizontal ScrollView with no indicator (632); maxHeight puts the body in a ScrollView under the header (597–610); with children it is composition and only a direct Table.Header is pinned (splitStickyHeaderChildren, 467); data [] renders the header only (523, 540); rows are a View with role row, or with onRowPress a Pressable with role row, tabIndex 0 on the web, Space through useKeyboardNavigation and opacity 0.6 while pressed (342–366); cells never truncate (Text's default layout wraps). Every guide sentence quoted here holds on dbe0e02. One does not: the #264 fix gives every string or number body cell the colour of tableHeader/label/color after Text's token colour (Table.tsx 108–110, 143; Text.tsx 153 puts style after the token colour), and that token is rgb(0, 0, 0) in every mode (Neutral, Success, Error, Secondary and Page type JioPlus resolved), so Text Appearance on the table no longer tints the values; only Coin Text that a column renders itself takes a Text Appearance (cloneChildrenWithModes merges the table's modes under its own). The 17 October re-check measured Weight, JioPlus and the roles, not Text Appearance. Left out for that reason, and listed in the human flag in reviews/table.json: Configuration's Status appearances card (“Success, Warning, and Error tint every body cell green, amber, or red; to mark one value, render your own cells.”); the Configuration description's “text size and the brand appearances are in the playground above” (the quote stops at “reach its body text only”, which still holds: no mode changes the header, the lines or the fills); the third Do & Don't pair, Colour single values / Colour the whole table, whose Don't caption “Text appearance on the table tints every value, so nothing stands out.” is false on this build (its Do caption is kept as a content rule); and the evidence's 12 October Text Appearance colours. Not recorded: the Sources note's “The app’s theme doesn’t reach the table, so it takes its modes directly” (true on dbe0e02: Table reads modes only from its own prop) and Color Mode, which the pack leaves to the brand team; the evidence's Not supported list (striping, sorting, selection and the rest), which the guide doesn't use; getRowKey, headerAlign and style (developer settings; the building rules keep style off Coin components); the composition API, recorded only as the children fact (same look, developer choice, as the evidence says); the Storybook page, its stories and Code Connect (Storybook-side, not usage gaps); Figma's hex values. TableColumn's fields (key, header, align, headerAlign, width, flex, render) are not facts in this release (show-facts lists none), so column items cite the guide or the evidence. Strengths: recommended or discouraged; nothing is required. Two quotes carry only: “Only the rows remain…” (everywhere: with showHeader false the header row is not drawn, Table.tsx 523) and “Modes on the table reach its body text only” (everywhere: the table's own tokens resolve the same in every mode). avoidWhen is empty: the guide names no case for another component, and the summary's “a few values” and the Narrow host advice (fewer columns or sideways scroll) are not avoid rules; the trace-check flags it. Anatomy: no part is marked always present: the header goes with showHeader false, rows and cells with no data (the No rows state), and Number is only in right-aligned number columns. The No rows state keeps the guide's “Put an Empty State next to it”, in the guide's words, so no placement edge to EmptyState is made (the Table is not placed in one). Content good keeps the guide's Recent payments headers and two formatted values; the guide shows no bad copy. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every Table and Text), no modes on the Table, no style (the guide's Host and Surface are docs frames); columns and data are inlined, since an example is one JSX expression (assemble wraps it in a fragment), and the row type is inferred from data. In context is the guide's portfolio screen: a VStack (the guide's Host is a stack) with a default Coin Text heading “Your holdings” (the guide's Text Sizes Large is dropped: no entry rule says a heading needs it) over the Table with the guide's COLOURED columns, whose Change render returns Coin Text with Text Appearance Error for a leading minus and Success otherwise, as the guide does: the only mode in the examples, set per value by the content rule from the Do “Colour single values” and Configuration's “Your own cells”; the empty onRowPress stands for the screen's navigation. Default and Column widths are the guide's Configuration cards with its HOLDINGS data and its COLUMNS and WIDTHS (Units centred, as the guide sets it; Column widths has no Change column, as in the guide, so each row's change field is unused). Text and VStack have entries (Text's is undocumented: facts only). Left out of examples: Without a header, Trimmed outer borders, the mode cards, the States, Sizing and Content cards, the Do & Don'ts and the playground. Gaps: the Sources note's Figma and code difference (Figma's single full-width header, a line under the header in code, taller rows; widths, alignment and scrolling only in code) and the evidence's 38 against 42 and 45 px rows. Sorting (batch 12, rounds 1–3): three cross-check runs. Round 1 flagged /examples/2 (Units centred, not in the copy) and /configuration/12 (the Don't “Fix widths that don't fit” targeted columnWidth, but applies to any fixed widths): the target is removed. Round 2 flagged /configuration/1 (“By default … numbers sit right” read as built in, while align defaults to left): now “In the guide's Default … the number columns are set to align right”; and /examples/2 again. Its note that the empty-data sentence dates from the first check is right (unchanged since 4fee471): that fact now carries 2026-10-12 and 0.1.78-636f3f5, and the 38/42/45 gap now says only what the evidence's Discrepancies line says. Round 3, on the final entry, flagged /examples/2 only: dismissed in reviews/table.json (the guide's own WIDTHS, table.guide.tsx line 43, rendered at line 105; the reviewer sees only the copy). Its notes, not flags: the unused change field (the guide's data, kept) and the core principle filed as a use-when (kept, as toggle.json does). Remaining: the trace-check flag on the empty avoidWhen, and the human flag on the Text Appearance sentences. Ticket (coordinator, batch 12): the guide fix is #534 (Documentation, To do), filed in this run with the four sentences above and the question whether black values under every Text Appearance are intended; the human flag names it. The coordinator confirmed the token: tableHeader/label/color resolves to rgb(0, 0, 0) with no modes, Text Appearance Success, Error and Secondary, and Page type JioPlus, while text/foreground follows Text Appearance.

examples.purpose: Holdings on a portfolio screen, the guide's In context: a heading over a Table whose Change column renders Coin Text, green for gains and red for losses (the Text Appearance comes from each value, as the guide's Do “Colour single values” shows); pressing a row opens that holding, and the screen handles the press. The empty press handler stands for the screen's own navigation.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Text>Your holdings</Text>
  <Table
    columns={[
      { key: 'asset', header: 'Asset' },
      { key: 'units', header: 'Units', align: 'right' },
      { key: 'value', header: 'Value', align: 'right' },
      {
        key: 'change',
        header: 'Change',
        align: 'right',
        render: (row) => (
          <Text modes={{ 'Text Appearance': row.change.startsWith('-') ? 'Error' : 'Success' }}>{row.change}</Text>
        ),
      },
    ]}
    data={[
      { asset: 'HDFC Bank', units: '120', value: '₹1,98,400', change: '+2.4%' },
      { asset: 'Reliance', units: '64', value: '₹1,52,900', change: '-0.8%' },
      { asset: 'Infosys', units: '210', value: '₹3,10,500', change: '+1.1%' },
      { asset: 'TCS', units: '48', value: '₹1,84,200', change: '+0.3%' },
    ]}
    onRowPress={(row) => {}}
  />
</VStack>

from.quote: The portfolio screen lists holdings with gains in green and losses in red. Pressing a row opens that holding; the screen handles the press.
